sanskrit: yat kṣīram upasicya prathamaṃ prāśnāti kilāsaḥ pratigrahītā bhavati ||
english: If, having poured milk over it, one eats first, the recipient becomes a kilāsa (one afflicted with a leprous skin disease).

sanskrit: yat sarpir upasicya prathamaṃ prāśnāti sarpaḥ pratigrahītāraṃ hanti ||
english: If, having poured ghee over it, one eats first, a serpent slays the recipient.

sanskrit: yan madhūpasicya prathamaṃ prāśnāti mahādevaḥ pratigrahītāraṃ hanti ||
english: If, having poured honey over it, one eats first, Mahādeva slays the recipient.

sanskrit: yan māṃsam upasicya prathamaṃ prāśnātīśānaḥ pratigrahītāraṃ hanti ||
english: If, having added meat to it, one eats first, Īśāna slays the recipient.

sanskrit: yad udakam upasicya prathamaṃ prāśnāti tat samṛddham | jyog jīvati sarvam āyur eti na purā jarasaḥ pramīyate ya evaṃ veda ||
english: If, having poured water over it, one eats first — that is prosperous. He lives long, reaches his full lifespan, and does not die before old age — he who knows thus.

sanskrit: yat prāśiṣyan purastād atimṛśati | prāṅ pratigrahītuḥ prāṇaḥ pra krāmati tata evotthāya pra vrajati śiras tasya rujatīti dvādaśīn nāti jīvaty evaṃ cainaṃ prāśnantam upadraṣṭā gṛhṇāti ||
english: If, while about to eat, one wipes the food from in front — the life-breath of the recipient goes forward; rising up from there it departs; his head aches. He does not live beyond twelve. And so an onlooker catches this person as he eats.

sanskrit: yat prāśiṣyan dakṣiṇataḥ pramṛśati | dakṣiṇā pratigrahītuḥ (…) ||
english: If, while about to eat, one wipes the food from the south — the recipient's [life-breath goes] to the right [southward — remainder as above, ellipsis in source].

sanskrit: yat prāśiṣyann uttarataḥ parimṛśaty udaṅ pratigrahītuḥ prāṇaḥ pra krāmati tata evotthāya pra vrajati śiras tasya rujatīti dvādaśīn nāti jīvaty evaṃ cainaṃ prāśnantam upadraṣṭā gṛhṇāti ||
english: If, while about to eat, one wipes the food from the north — the life-breath of the recipient goes northward; rising up from there it departs; his head aches. He does not live beyond twelve. And so an onlooker catches this person as he eats.

sanskrit: yat prāśiṣyan paścāt prāñcam abhimṛśati | śarmaṇā caivainaṃ tad varmaṇā cābhi mṛśati śarma caivāsmai varma ca bhavati jayaty odanam odanaloko bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
english: If, while about to eat, one wipes it from behind forward — one thereby touches it with shelter and with armor. Both shelter and armor come to be his. He conquers the rice-dish; he becomes one whose world is the rice-dish — he who knows thus.

sanskrit: indrasyauja sthendrasya saha sthendrasya balaṃ stha- -indrasya nṛmṇaṃ sthendrasya śukraṃ sthendrasya vīryaṃ stha | jiṣṇave yogāyendrayogair vo yunajmi jiṣṇave yogāya viśvāni mā rūpāṇy upa tiṣṭhantu yuktā ma āpa stha ||
english: Ye are Indra's vital force; ye are Indra's might; ye are Indra's strength; ye are Indra's heroic power; ye are Indra's brilliance; ye are Indra's virility. For victorious yoking I yoke you with the yokings of Indra. For victorious yoking, may all forms attend upon me. Yoked to me, ye Waters, stand here.
[As 16.127.1, with:] I yoke you with the yokings of kṣatra for victorious yoking [remainder as 16.127.1, ellipsis in source].
[As 16.127.1, with:] I yoke you with the yokings of brahman for victorious yoking [remainder as 16.127.1, ellipsis in source].
[As 16.127.1, with:] I yoke you with the yokings of food (anna) for victorious yoking [remainder as 16.127.1, ellipsis in source].

sanskrit: indrasyauja sthendrasya saha sthendrasya balaṃ stha- -indrasya nṛmṇaṃ sthendrasya śukraṃ sthendrasya vīryaṃ stha | jiṣṇave yogāyāpāṃ yogair vo yunajmi jiṣṇave yogāya viśvāni mā rūpāṇy upa tiṣṭhantu yuktā ma āpa stha ||
english: Ye are Indra's vital force; ye are Indra's might; ye are Indra's strength; ye are Indra's heroic power; ye are Indra's brilliance; ye are Indra's virility. For victorious yoking I yoke you with the yokings of the Waters. For victorious yoking, may all forms attend upon me. Yoked to me, ye Waters, stand here.
